title: Apple's Deal With Dialog Semiconductor Show It's Betting Its Chips on Chips
text:
Apple’s Deal With Dialog Semiconductor Show It’s Betting Its Chips on Chips By Updated Oct. 11, 2018 2:06 p.m. ET Order Reprints Tomohiro Ohsumi/Getty Images) Text size
The chip business may not be as exciting as iPhones or original content, but it’s of increasing importance to Apple (ticker: AAPL), which has been looking for more ways to tighten control over its supply chain and use custom chips to introduce new features.
The company appeared to have made another move in that direction on Thursday. Dialog Semiconductor (DLGNF), a longtime Apple chip supplier, said in a release that it has struck a deal with the smartphone giant through which Apple will pay $300 million in cash to license technologies, obtain some Dialog assets, and bring on more than 300 Dialog employees.
Apple will also prepay for $300 million in Dialog products. Apple uses Dialog’s products mainly for power management, charging, and audio functions. Newsletter Sign-up
“We are thrilled to have this talented group of engineers who’ve long supported our products now working directly for Apple,” Johny Srouji, Apple’s senior vice president for hardware technologies, said in a statement. Apple didn’t respond to a Barron’s request for comment on Dialog’s release.
Dialog said that the engineers heading to Apple were already supporting the smartphone manufacturer’s chip-development efforts. Having more in-house chip designers may make it easier for Apple to ensure that its hardware supports its overall goals.
According to the Wall Street Journal, the addition of 300 employees through an acquisition is one of the largest such moves in Apple’s history.
The company made its custom chips a key focus of its iPhone launch event last month. Apple spent a solid chunk of its presentation discussing how its A12 Bionic chip would enable enhanced capabilities on its latest line of iPhones. The new chip helps users take better smartphone photos, engage in more intense gaming, and explore augmented reality. Artificial intelligence helps make the functions possible .
For Apple, AI is one way to sweeten the appeal of its ecosystem of devices. Smarter cameras and applications are subtle ways that the company can keep current iPhone users loyal and draw in new customers. By designing its own chips, the company can tailor its hardware specifically to features it deems crucial.
Apple shares were roughly flat as of midafternoon Thursday. The stock closed at $216.36 in the prior session, off 4.6%.
This story was updated since it was first published to account for share price movement.
